issue.title: GenericFlag validators panic with standard-library flag.Getter values
issue.body:
## My urfave/cli version is

Reproduced on the latest release, **v3.14.0**, and current main at **26bd9a28850d7276700f83bd6bf0b8c763f12cdc**.

## Checklist

- [x] Reproduced on the latest v3 release.
- [x] Checked the v3 manual and the Value/GenericFlag interfaces.
- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs for GenericFlag, Getter and validator failures.

## Dependency Management

Go modules.

## Describe the bug

A GenericFlag can accept a value from Go's standard flag package, then panic before calling its Validator. The value satisfies cli.Value, but its Get method returns a string. GenericFlag unwraps that string and then tries to assert it back to cli.Value.

## To reproduce

Save this as main.go:

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"

	cli "github.com/urfave/cli/v3"
)

func main() {
	std := flag.NewFlagSet("std", flag.ContinueOnError)
	std.String("value", "", "")

	cmd := &cli.Command{
		Flags: []cli.Flag{&cli.GenericFlag{
			Name:      "value",
			Value:     std.Lookup("value").Value.(cli.Value),
			Validator: func(cli.Value) error { return nil },
		}},
	}
	_ = cmd.Run(context.Background(), []string{"app", "--value", "hello"})
}

```

Run in an empty directory:

```sh
go mod init example.com/cli-getter-repro
go get github.com/urfave/cli/v3@v3.14.0
go run .
```

## Observed behavior

```text
panic: interface conversion: string is not cli.Value: missing method Get
```

The panic occurs at the typed Validator call in FlagBase.Set. The Validator body is never reache

My impression is that you're satisfying the interface but the validator is rejecting it a few steps down, so the solve is to either tighten the interface or loosen the validator. Im not opinionated on which one is better.

comments.author: MohammediYunus
comments.body: Thanks for taking a look! I’ve opened #2460 with a fix that keeps the existing interface and Command.Value behaviour. It handles payload-returning Getters in validation, flag actions and Command.Generic, with regression tests for each. Happy to adjust after review.
